title: Tenant-aware routing and prioritization policy for console/reporting requests
creator: Aisha Rodriguez
description: Define and implement a tenant-aware intake, scoring, and routing policy for Console reporting requests (usage analytics, cost breakdowns, exports, and dashboards). Aim is to ensure enterprise requests (large exports, custom dashboards, high-frequency cost reports) are prioritized by SLA band, routed to the correct engineering or Solutions team queue, and surfaced with billing impact and data sensitivity metadata. This ticket covers product decisions, intake schema, prioritized routing rules, and the handoff artifacts for ENG to implement the routing filters and for Console to add UI flags and reviewer flows.
acceptance_criteria: An intake schema (JSON) that captures tenant_size, request_type, expected_rows, export_format, data_sensitivity, requested_sla, and customer_tier is finalized and published.
A scoring matrix that maps intake fields to priority bands (P0/P1/P2) is documented and reviewed by ENG and Solutions.
Routing rules that assign requests to queues (Self-serve / Solutions / Engineering / Security review) are defined and published.
A prototype router implemented in staging that demonstrates correct routing for 10 representative enterprise scenarios with automated tests.
Cost impact estimator displays an approximate token/compute cost for large exports and is included in the intake confirmation.
All stakeholder approvals obtained (PM, Eng, Design, Security, CS) and a handoff doc with implementation tasks created for ENG-3210.
Telemetry events defined for intake-submitted, routed-to-queue, routed-decision, and routing-fallback and visible in our sandbox dashboard.
Rollout plan with feature flag and gradual enablement to top 50 enterprise workspaces in first wave is agreed.
plan: Week 1: Draft intake schema and scoring matrix; workshop with Solutions and CS to capture common enterprise request patterns.
Week 2: Align with Security/Compliance on data_sensitivity taxonomy and KMS/HSM gating requirements.
Week 3: Design routing DSL with ENG for queue filters and fallbacks; create staging prototype for 10 scenarios.
Week 4: Implement telemetry and cost estimator integration; add UI flag and confirmation text in Console.
Week 5: Sign-off from stakeholders; create GH PRs and handoff tickets for production rollout under feature flag.
Week 6: Gradual rollout, monitoring, and adjustment based on false positives and SLA misses.
decisions: Use a tenant_size (monthly_tokens) + expected_rows heuristic to escalate export requests into higher SLA bands.
Export formats supported at launch: CSV, Parquet; large exports >10M rows default to async job with email webhook.
Data sensitivity levels (public, internal, restricted) determine whether a security review queue is required.
Charge-back estimate shown to user during intake; definitive billing handled post-export via existing usage pipeline.
Route non-enterprise, low-cost requests to self-serve queue to preserve Solutions/ENG capacity.
Requests without required fields fall back to manual triage and receive a 'needs info' status.
Feature flag gating for 6-week staged rollout restricted to enterprise tier workspaces.
open_questions: What exact thresholds define tenant_size buckets for medium vs large? (finance input required)
Do we need per-tenant rate limits for exports at the platform layer or per-request throttling is sufficient?
How should we tag routed issues in Linear vs internal ticketing used by Solutions Engineering?
Is there a legal/regulatory constraint for on-prem/private (VPC) customers that changes routing?
Should the scoring matrix be editable by Support via a limited Console view for triage overrides?
notes: 2026-01-22: Workshop notes added — common enterprise asks include scheduled cost exports, per-team cost breakdowns, and multi-region usage CSVs. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CR/PM-18421+workshop
2026-02-05: Security scoped data_sensitivity taxonomy and provided initial gating rules (restricted -> security review).
2026-02-18: Design sketches (DES-412) propose an intake modal with estimated cost and SLA badge visible before submission.
2026-02-28: ENG spike (ENG-3210) produced prototype router service and unit tests for routing DSL.
2026-03-09: Pre-alpha staging validation passed for 8/10 test scenarios; two cases require additional headers for tenant identification.
acceptance_risks: Misclassification of tenant_size could push too many requests to engineering and increase operational load.
Underestimating cost for large exports could create billing disputes with customers.
Routing logic complexity may make debugging triage decisions harder for Support unless we log full decision context.
Security review queue could become a bottleneck without staffing plans from Security team.
Privacy/regulatory edge cases for EU/UK customers require legal review before full rollout.
rollout_notes: Start behind feature flag for enterprise cohorts (top 50 by ARR) and Solutions-managed accounts.
Monitor routing-fallback and SLA-miss rates for first 14 days; rollback flag if >5% critical SLA misses.
Provide CS playbook for triage overrides and customer messaging templates for expected wait times.
Schedule a post-mortem and tuning session after wave 1 to update thresholds and add missing metadata to intake.
Require Security sign-off before enabling 'restricted' processing for customer data exports.
